I would like to do Advent of Code with Roc again this year.

I plan to use the built-in echo platform. I really like the idea that all the code for a single day is contained in one file.

A template could look like this:

template file

import "day00.input" as puzzle_input : Str

main! = |args| {
    result = match parse_args(args) {
        Part1 => day1(puzzle_input)?
        Part2 => day2(puzzle_input)?
        Both => {
            "day1: ${day1(puzzle_input)?}\n\nday2:${day2(puzzle_input)?}"
        }
        Help(message) => message
    }
    echo!("${result}\n")
    Ok({})
}

day1 = |_input| {
    Ok("day1 - TODO")
}

day2 = |_input| {
    Ok("day2 - TODO")
}

example_input =
    \\Example Input

expect {
    got = day1(example_input)?

    got == example_input
}

# expect {
#   got = day2(example_input)?
#
#   got == example_input
# }

parse_args = |args| {
    if args.contains("-h") {
        message =
            \\Solution for aoc2026
            \\
            \\The default is to run the solution for both parts. To only run one part, use the arguments `1` or `2`.
        Help(message)
    } else if args.contains("1") {
        Part1
    } else if args.contains("2") {
        Part2
    } else {
        Both
    }
}

My impression is that there's fewer people interested in AoC, but the people interested in it are doing weirder stuff with their solutions. Like solving problems in the gnu calculator or whatever.

I do AoC to learn a new language every year. This time it's Roc. I'm confused though, what do you mean by "echo platform"? I thought basic-cli and basic-webserver are platforms, and I don't see any platform import in your repos. Also, I don't see why a platform is needed for AOC-style problems.

Roc has a default or builtin platform that is very simple and has only a single effect, echo! which prints to stdout. It's available without a URL to download or reference a platform -- like a platform-less (or even headerless if you want) app.

This is a complete file... example.roc

main! = |_args| {
    echo!("Hello world")
    Ok({})
}

$ ~/roc-macos_apple_silicon-0.1.0_RC1/roc example.roc
Hello world
You could use this for AoC if you wanted... pair it with import for your input file https://www.roc-lang.org/examples/IngestFiles/README and you should be off to the races

Understood, thanks! I know I could do echo! without a platform, in my mind that was the "platform-less" setup. Thanks for the clarification.

And btw, this import is a cool feature!

https://www.roc-lang.org/examples/IngestFiles/README 

import "some-file.txt" as some_str : Str
import "some-file" as some_bytes : List(U8)

Interesting, can one do this?

import "some-file.txt" as some_lines : List(Str)
I think it needs to be Str or List(U8)

Sincen roc has comptime evaluation, you can import the file as str and then write 

as_lines = some_str.split_on("\n")
haha, if you're not careful the whole solution might be ran at compile time :sweat_smile:

Interesting point. I'm curious, any hints what would stop the compiler from evaluating everything at compile time. i.e. when the input got imported it is hardcoded and by the nature of aoc I would suspect that the result is determenistic from its input so what should stop compile time evaluation?

if you make it a thunk then call it at runtime, so I think something like this

import ... as some_str : Str

my_runtime_calc = || { ... # do something with some_str }

main! = || { ...

my_runtime_calc is a lambda/function .. so it wont be evaluated until runtime when you call it
I'm not sure though... the semantics around these features as evolved a lot. I would probably test it out using basic-cli and some clock measurements. But its getting late here.

Ah, yes I might should have guessed that.
No need to try I guess 1 Dez will give us the chance to find out.
Basically who can get all aoc solutiouns run with the same max time which is technically only printing the result :joy:

I'm also looking forward to trying out Roc for AoC this year (it will be my first time using the language)!

I do have several questions though, namely:

  1. Are there any meaningful downsides to using the echo platform, or will it be (more than?) sufficient for AoC?
  2. The Str class is still a bit of a mystery to me -- would it be best to just use List(U8) for AoC things?
  3. How do people manage Roc versions? With the impending 0.1.0 release (and patches leading up to it) this is something I want to be conscious of.
  4. Are there any good repos/projects/whatever to reference to get a feel of Roc? I learn best by doing (thus doing AoC) but some pattern matching is always helpful.

I guess these questions may be better(?) suited for the #beginners channel... let me know if I should post there instead.

In regards to 1: It's definitely not needed. The only reason I used the basic-cli platform in my AoC harness is to have access to the Utc module for measuring time. Otherwise it only uses Stdout, which is what echo does.

Hi @Jake Keller,

  1. The Str class is still a bit of a mystery to me -- would it be best to just use List(U8) for AoC things?

Are there any good repos/projects/whatever to reference to get a feel of Roc?

I forgot to mention, but the possibility of solving the whole puzzle at comptime is pretty cool. My friends and I sometimes compete on solution speed as well... so that could be quite a fun party trick :smile:
